 La Liga leaderBarcelona hosts Alaves on Saturday as it looks to respond to its first defeat of the domestic season.
 Barcelona’s lead atop La Liga has been cut down to just two points as Alavés prepares to visit on Saturday in the hopes of handing Hansi Flick’s a second straight loss. Barca was enjoying an unblemished campaign in the truest sense until last weekend, and Basque outfit Alavés can capitalize after edging a 1-0 upset the last time these two teams met in the reverse fixture back in May. El Glorioso makes its way to Catalonia sat seventh in Spain’s top flight despite failing to win any of its last six games and taking just two points from the last 18 on offer.

 Live stream the Barcelona vs Alavés game on Fubo: Start Watching Now! 
 After nine straight wins, Barcelona’s perfect run atop La Liga finally came to an end last week after losing 2-1 at home to Jose Mourinho’s Real Madrid.
 El Clasico has been dominated by Los Cules in recent years, but Los Blancos breathed new life into the title battle after winning at the Camp Nou for the first time since 2023:
 That also marked Barca’s second consecutive defeat in all competitions after losing 4-2 at Paris Saint-Germain in the Champions League just five days prior.
 This could go one of two ways for Alavés, who will either face a Barca side lacking confidence, or one that’s newly invigorated to reopen its lead in the wake of recent disappointments.
 La Liga veteran Quique Sanchez Flores boasts extensive experience coaching in Spain’s top flight over the past 20 years or so, and the former Real right-back will have undoubtedly enjoyed last weekend’s outcome at the Camp Nou.
 However, he’s won just five of his 20 managerial battles against Barca and has never managed to get one over the Catalan kings at the Camp Nou.
 Left-back Xavi Espart has joined Flick’s list of absentees with an ankle injury that could keep him out for around six weeks, with Alejandro Balde likely to take his place while Joao Cancelo moves to right-back.
